names_for.catalogue_side: Datasets (the Hugging Face Hub's dataset repositories; 'gated datasets' for access-controlled ones)
names_for.custom_side: none found: no bespoke data-collection offer was seen on the pricing page or Hub docs

operator_role.note: Hugging Face hosts; the uploader keeps ownership, sets the licence and grants it; HF takes only a licence to provide the service.

economics_model.note: No per-dataset sale or fee: downloads are free. HF monetises hosting (subscriptions, storage, compute) paid by uploaders and teams, not transactions.

who_pays_fee.note: No transaction fee exists; storage and plan fees fall on the account that hosts or uses them.

supply_models.note: Open uploads by any account; organisations such as NVIDIA and GenRobot publish their own datasets; HF's own team publishes web-scraped corpora such as FineWeb.

custody_model.note: Files sit in HF's Xet/Git storage and are served via CDN; users download or clone copies. Some third-party datasets are links-only, but the Hub's model is hosting.

transaction_mode.note: Free download, optionally behind an author-run access gate; no checkout.

public_prices.note: Datasets carry no price; only plans and storage are priced.

licence_model.note: Each author picks a licence identifier or a custom 'other' licence; gated datasets can require acceptance of the provider's own agreement.

exclusivity_offered.note: No exclusivity mechanism found; the licences seen (open licences, NVIDIA's) are non-exclusive, but off-platform deals cannot be ruled out.

public_listing.note: Public dataset pages and cards are open to anonymous visitors; gated datasets show the card but files require an account and accepted request; private datasets are hidden.

buyer_vetting.note: HF itself checks nothing beyond an account for gated files; each author chooses no gate, an automatic gate, or manual approval with custom fields.

sample_mechanics.note: Data Studio shows rows, column distributions and SQL over the first 5GB of large non-Parquet datasets.

versioning.note: Git commits give pinnable revisions and DOIs can freeze a version, but the default branch is mutable and owners can squash history or delete repos.

human_subject_consent_docs.note: The platform asks for no consent evidence; the card template invites an optional personal-information statement, and the uploader's warranty runs to HF, not to downloaders.

contributor_pay_model.note: Nothing is sold, so uploaders are not paid; the licence they grant HF is royalty-free.

catalogue_plus_custom.note: Hosting and discovery of ready-made datasets only; no collect-to-order offer found.

erasure_after_sale.note: HF can remove or disable content and authors can revoke gated access, but no platform term obliges downloaders to delete copies; some provider licences (e.g. NVIDIA's) do.

quality_evidence.note: Quality statements are the author's own card text; HF supplies an automatic viewer and statistics but does not verify claims.

Q1.answer: Usage is measured in developers and downloads, not purchases: HF-side counts of hosted datasets range from 500k public to over 1M, with 18M+ developers; no data on paying buyers or units exists because access is free.

Q2.answer: Providers get free public hosting, a rendered card, an in-browser viewer, library integrations and an audience; HF asks in return that large datasets be useful for community reuse and charges for private and above-quota storage.

Q3.answer: Inventory comes from any account holder's uploads, from organisations publishing their own datasets (NVIDIA, GenRobot) and from HF's own scraped corpora; each is listed on the uploader's own warranty of rights and chosen licence.

Q4.answer: HF commissions no data and sells none, so there is no resale carve-out; no after-the-fact change to uploader terms was found (ToS dated 2022-09-15).

Q5.answer: HF is a venue: uploaders own their content, warrant their rights to HF, choose the licence and indemnify HF, which disclaims all warranties; the licensor of record is the dataset author.

Q6.answer: Platform-hosted: datasets are Xet-backed Git repositories on HF storage, served via CDN, and users download, clone or stream copies to their own machines.

Q7.answer: The platform requires no consent evidence from capturers, subjects or property owners; the uploader warrants rights, the content policy bars publishing others' private information without permission, and the card template invites an optional personal-data statement. Individual providers add their own terms (NVIDIA data-subject cooperation, FineWeb PII removal form).

Q8.answer: Licences are author-defined (open licences or custom text); HF offers gating with custom acceptance fields, EU geo-blocking, access revocation and JSON access reports, but no fingerprinting or audit; downloaded copies are outside its control except where a provider licence demands destruction.

Q9.answer: No deals close on HF: access is a free download, optionally behind an author-run gate with automatic or manual approval; HF earns from subscriptions and storage, not commission.

Q10.answer: A dataset is a Git repository with a README card; versions are commits, branches or tags loadable by revision, and DOIs can pin a revision. Entitlements are per-user gate approvals that the author can reset or revoke; owners can squash history.

Q11.answer: Before downloading, anyone can read the dataset card and browse rows, distributions and SQL results in Data Studio; gated datasets still show the card. Quality evidence is the author's own card.

Q12.answer: Only the catalogue side exists: 'Datasets' on the Hub. No bespoke collection offer was found on pricing or Hub documentation pages.

claims.statement: A Hugging Face dataset author can switch the gate to manual approval and accept or reject each pending request.

sources.quote: If you want to manually approve which users can access your dataset, you must set it to **manual approval**.

conflicts.resolution: Same-day sources: TechCrunch says Nvidia 'has acquired' Hugging Face, while NVIDIA's own 8-K describes a definitive agreement expected to close in H1 2027. The filing's wording is taken; status stays active pending close.
Dataset counts differ: 500k public (docs and TechCrunch), 1.5M (docs header), 1,069,830 (live directory). Definitions (public vs all) are not stated.

leads.why: Census lead: Business Insider reported on 2026-08-24 that Hugging Face was exploring a sale at $13B+; the site refused automated fetch.
Reported July 2026 security incident on HF servers (from Wikipedia's references); not fetched.
Independent report of the 2023 $235M round at $4.5B; not fetched.
Gating Group Collections for Team/Enterprise; org-level access management.
Mutable, non-versioned storage buckets, a second custody model alongside Git repos.
